Hon'ble Rajiv Gupta,J.
1.

Sri Ashutosh Pandey, Advocate has filed short counter affidavit alongwith the vakalatnama on
behalf of opposite party No. 2 today in Court, which is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State, learned counsel for the opposite party No. 2 and perused the record.
3.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with a prayer to quash the charge sheet dated 17.5.2022 and cognizance/summoning order dated 2.7.2022 as well as further proceedings of Case No. 29279 of 2022 (State Vs. Nand Kishor and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 04 of Nand Koshor And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123356679/
1 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District- Mathura, pending in the court of Civil Judge (J.D.), Fast Track Court (Crime against Women),
Judicial Magistrate, Mathura.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that opposite party No. 2 is the wife of applicant No. 1 and applicant Nos. 2 and 3 are the father in-law and mother in-law of opposite party No. 2.

Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that on account of matrimonial discord, the present criminal case was instituted against the applicants by the opposite party No. 2, however with the intervention of the respected members of both the families and society, they have amicably settled all their disputes and differences and now they do not have any grievance against each other.

5. Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that a compromise application dated 16.6.2023 supported by an affidavit has been drawn between the parties, a copy of which has been annexed as Annexue No. 5 to this application.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant has next submitted that other cases filed between the parties under Section 125 Cr.P.C. and under Section 12 of Domestic Violence Act has also been decided on the basis of compromise.
7. Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that in view of the compromise made between the parties, entire proceedings be quashed.

8. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has also appeared and has filed an affidavit on behalf of opposite party No. 2 and in paragraph-3 of the said affidavit, the factum of compromise has been reiterated.

In paragraph-5 of the said affidavit, it is further stated that in view of the compromise,
she does not want to further pursue the present proceeding.

It is further stated thatshe has no objection if the entire proceedings are quashed.
9.

This Court is not unmindful of the judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of :-
1. B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 SCC 675.
2. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation [2008) 9 SCC 677].
3. Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others ( 2008) 16 SCC 1.
4. Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303.
5. Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab ( 2014) 6 SCC 466.

sentences.text: 10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, and also the submissions made by the counsel for the parties, the court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose shall be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned case.

11. Accordingly, the entire proceedings of Case No. 29279 of 2022 (State Vs. Nand Kishor and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 04 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District- Mathura, pending in the court of Civil Judge (J.D.), Fast Track Court (Crime against Women), Judicial Magistrate, Mathura, are hereby quashed.
